proof_attempt_summary: Discovery repaired the model's observed-outcome law and completed the matched rate arguments and explicit positive-law witnesses. The math referee passed, while the general referee assigned subfield with a 6.9 score ceiling below the required field threshold of 7.4; the accepted-bank comparison remained an editorial gap. No Lean formalization began, and a field-tier result would require a substantially broader matched frontier or genuine application.
tldr: Within the balanced binary latent benchmark, dose-local smoothing contributes squared risk \((n\sigma^2)^{-4/5}\) and common-agreement calibration contributes \((n\sigma^4)^{-1}\). The data-only clipped estimator and connected bias-budget interval attain the capped risk and honest-length orders. One proved positive causal-law pair supplies the dose-local lower bound, and a second proved positive causal-law pair supplies the calibration lower bound. Those witnesses satisfy Ham--Wu--Cui Assumptions A--B, so the lower converses transfer to every HWC-style class containing them; the matching upper bounds remain specific to the binary benchmark. Supplying channel strength removes the calibration term at rate level. The simultaneous local-global Le Cam limit experiment at the crossover, its nuisance-projected sharp modulus constant, and an attaining shortest 95%-honest connected interval remain open.
gap: Current proximal dose inference assumes a regular bridge regime, while generic unknown-operator minimax theory observes calibration in a separate Gaussian experiment. Neither determines whether dose and outcome cells can improve calibration, nor gives an honest interval converse over positive causal laws when proxy accuracy shrinks.
fill: The project derives an exact observed-moment inversion, constructs a globally pooled and locally smoothed estimator, and matches it with two positive causal lower paths plus a known-channel oracle comparison.
